title: The Projects Are Advancing. The Guarantees Are Thinning.
method: AI-assisted cross-source synthesis with direct links to originating publishers. Reviewed against a six-item gate including two primary institutional sources.

items.headline: Uganda begins a phased withdrawal from Somalia
items.whyItMatters: The timetable turns Somalia’s security transition into a capacity test with a fixed horizon. The unresolved point is whether Somali forces and remaining partners can cover areas vulnerable to al-Shabaab as Ugandan contingents depart.

items.source: Office of the United States Trade Representative
items.headline: United States intends to remove Rwanda from AGOA on January 1
items.whyItMatters: The decision would deepen Rwanda’s existing partial exclusion from the preference programme and add policy risk for exporters using U.S. market access. Implementation is prospective until the stated effective date.

items.headline: Ethiopia and Sudan close each other’s border consulates
items.whyItMatters: Consulate closures remove local diplomatic capacity precisely where cross-border security and humanitarian risks are rising. The governments’ competing allegations remain disputed and have not been independently adjudicated.

items.headline: World Bank raises Kenya’s 2026 growth forecast while naming governance as a binding constraint
items.whyItMatters: The update links governance directly to the price of capital rather than treating it as a separate institutional issue. Forecasts remain estimates, and the government disputes the Bank’s growth projection as too low.

items.headline: Kenyan tribunal dismisses challenge to Dangote’s planned Lamu refinery
items.whyItMatters: The decision removes one legal obstacle from a project that could reshape regional fuel supply and public-sector exposure. It does not settle other approvals, financing terms, government participation or the construction timetable.

items.headline: EAC records faster cargo transit and stronger African exports while pressing for trade-finance reform
items.whyItMatters: The record supplies measurable evidence that integration can reduce time costs and expand markets, while identifying finance and border friction as the next constraints. The release does not specify the export comparison period or provide a new implementation timetable for the proposed reforms.
